direction: Decouple depot-start boundary selection (current_node == depot) from mid-route scoring (current_node != depot) using strictly scale-invariant (dimensionless) terms.
hypothesis: H-003: Decoupling the depot-start boundary from moderate mid-route depot pull (alpha_mid ~ 0.6) removes the +8% inside-out deadhead trap of C/V0 while preserving scale invariance and beating all four explicit seeds (A, B, C, V0).

operations.mechanism: When starting a new route from the depot, evaluate candidates using a scale-free outside-in / radial-load seed rule instead of letting linear d_cur - alpha*d_dep (alpha<1) pick the nearest customer or letting savings=0 degenerate to an arbitrary tie-break.

Keep moderate depot pull (alpha_mid around 0.5-0.8, or dimensionless ratio d_cur / scale - alpha * d_dep / scale) combined with scale-free capacity-fill terms (demand / rest_capacity) that stay invariant when coordinates are scaled by 0.01 or 1000.
Eliminate absolute length constants like +1.0 in near-tie bands and unit-mixing ratios like |rest_capacity - dem| / d_cur that diverge as O(1/s^2) under coordinate rescaling.
operations.target: mixed-unit constants and raw demand/distance ratios

preserve: Exact select_next_node signature, feasibility, numpy-only fast execution, and strong nominal performance without regressing below the best explicit seed.

research_activity.decision_summary: Split select_next_node cleanly at current_node == depot: use a scale-free far or radial-plus-load depot-start rule, and at current_node != depot combine moderate depot pull (alpha_mid ~ 0.5-0.8) with strictly dimensionless capacity-fill modulation (functions of demand/rest_capacity and distance ratios). Avoid any absolute length offset (+1.0) or raw demand/distance division.
research_activity.finding_summary: Boundary analysis across 72 multi-scale CVRP instances (n=50/100/200) proved an exact depot-start phase transition at alpha=1 for s(i,j)=d(i,j)-alpha*d(0,j): at i=0, s(0,j)=(1-alpha)*d(0,j), so alpha<1 (C, V0 with 0.6) always starts inside-out (nearest customer, dist percentile 0.006), inflating return-leg deadhead from 23.7% to 33.6%. Crossing alpha=0.99->1.01 drops route length discontinuously by -6.82%. Counterfactual swaps changing ONLY i=0 to far or heavy-far drop V0 from 20.30 to 18.61 (-8.29%), beating A (18.90), B (19.08), and savings (18.91). Also, A degenerates at i=0 to min-demand (dist percentile 0.484), and C's cap_term=|rest_cap-dem|/d_cur blows up as O(1/s^2) under rescaling.
research_activity.question: Why do C and V0 (alpha=0.6) lose ~8% across scales while A and B generalize, and what happens if we decouple the depot-start boundary?
